detail:
WHAT IT IS
Phase Two of the Royal Saudi Air Force's King Saud Air Base (383 sq km, Hafr Al-Batin, Eastern Region). Owner: Ministry of Defence (RSAF is named as the government entity on Etimad). MEED (10 Sep 2026): 'Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Defence & Aviation has started the tendering process for the next phase of the King Saud Air Base in the kingdom. Contractors have been given until 20 October to submit their bids. The scope of works covers the construction of the headquarters building, administrative buildings, operations and maintenance area, police camp facilities, weapons and ammunition area, residential facilities, airfield facilities and other associated facilities. The project duration is three years.' (https://guest.meed.com/saudi-arabia-tenders-next-phase-of-king-saud-air-base/). Construction Review Online (10 Sep 2026) adds that the tender follows 'an earlier qualification process for the design and construction of Phase Two facilities' and that the qualification scope 'also included power generation, water and wastewater pumping stations, and fiber-optic communications'. It gives qualification ref. 241140017394 and names Dar AlRiyadh as project consultant (https://constructionreviewonline.com/king-saud-air-base-1-36-billion-phase-two-construction-tender-moves-saudi-project-forward/). The base was launched in March 2016 (foundation stone laid by King Salman) as a three-phase redevelopment of the former advanced air base (SPA, https://www.spa.gov.sa/1475763). An earlier master plan by Stanley Consultants, for client USACE Middle East District, notes the base 'needed extensive utility infrastructure such as power plants, pumping stations, roads, water and sewer' (https://www.stanleyconsultants.com/solutions/planning-consulting/project/king-saud-air-base).

PHASE ONE / SISTER PACKAGES (who holds the power scope today)
- Phase One: about SR6.6bn ($1.8bn), awarded 'early last year' (i.e. early 2025). Package 1 (~SR2.9bn/$783m) went to a JV of Isam Khairi Kabbani Group and Alfanar Projects. Package 2 (~$1bn) went to Albawani, Shibh Al-Jazira Contracting and Kuwait's Alghanim International (MEED, same url).
- Petrojet (Egypt) won a SAR600m ($160m) contract in Sept 2025 for 'civil works at King Saud Air Base ... connections, protection, and electrical networks, as well as sewage and water lines linked to a power plant'. The work is in partnership with Alfanar and Isam Khairi Kabbani Group, with an 18-month completion (Mubasher, 14 Sep 2025, https://en.sharikatmubasher.com/media-hub/news/21506235/egypts-petrojet-wins-160mn-contract-in-saudi-arabia?lang=en). So a base power plant already sits in the Phase One Kabbani/Alfanar scope. The genset or engine brand of that plant is NOT public. Whether it is diesel, gas or grid-backed is also not public.
- MEP subcontractors and genset brands on Phase One: not found in any public source (checked MEED guest API, Construction Review, Mubasher, web search in English and Arabic).

SCOPE & RATINGS
- Public sources give no genset schedule, count or kVA. The qualification scope lists 'power generation' plus water and wastewater pumping stations. From that (INFERENCE), the Phase Two contractor supplies (a) generation or standby for the new HQ/admin, O&M, police camp, weapons and ammunition and residential zones, and (b) standby at each pumping station, tied into the Phase One power plant and networks.
- Frequency: Saudi Arabia is 60 Hz (230/400 V LV). Sets must therefore be the 60 Hz range (Cummins 'D6' models, e.g. C2000D6 = 2,000 kWe standby / 1,825 kWe prime on QSK60), NOT the D5 (50 Hz) models listed in the earlier record.
- Site conditions (INFERENCE): Hafr Al-Batin summer ambient reaches about 50 C, so specs will call for high-ambient cooling (50-55 C) and derated outputs, plus desert filtration.
- Standards (INFERENCE, not confirmed): the MoD/RSAF MEP spec for this package is not public. Historic RSAF bases were planned under USACE (per Stanley), so specs may cite US/NFPA practice (NFPA 110 Level 1 for life-safety/critical, UFC-style prime/standby definitions) alongside SBC 401 (IEC-based). Ask Dar AlRiyadh which spec book applies.

DATES & PROCESS
- Qualification (Etimad ref. 241140017394) completed earlier. The bid is restricted to qualified firms.
- Bid submission: 20 Oct 2026 (MEED). No extension reported as of 29 Sep 2026.
- Contract: design-and-build, 3 years.
- Tender number, document fee, site-visit and pre-bid dates are not public (Etimad restricted).

COMMERCIAL TERMS (general Saudi rules, not tender-specific)
- Saudi Government Tenders & Procurement Law norms: initial (bid) guarantee typically 1-2% of bid value and final (performance) guarantee 5%. NOT verified for this tender.
- LCGPA local content: a price preference for local products and a mandatory list apply to government purchases. Whether diesel gensets are on the current LCGPA Mandatory List is NOT confirmed (searches found tiles, pumps, valves, cables and split ACs, not gensets). Either way, a local-content certificate score and local packaging help in evaluation. From 1 Aug 2026, mandatory-list items also need a minimum enterprise local-content score (SPA, https://www.spa.gov.sa/en/N2514218).

ELIGIBILITY
- Bid only by firms qualified under ref. 241140017394. The qualified list is not public. Phase One winners (Kabbani/Alfanar; Albawani/Shibh Al-Jazira/Alghanim) are the obvious likely qualifiers (INFERENCE).
- Genset vendors will need MoD vendor approval or approval inside the contractor's submittal. Security clearance for site personnel is likely (INFERENCE).

COMPETITORS (brand via bidder; all INFERENCE unless stated)
- Alfanar (Phase One incumbent) is a large electrical manufacturer and EPC. It will buy sets from a packager, and incumbency on the Phase One power plant gives it a brand-standardisation argument. Brand unknown.
- Caterpillar via Zahid Tractor is the default rival on MoD and large-base work.
- mtu (Rolls-Royce) is likely where the Phase One plant or critical loads use high-speed 16/20V sets.
- Local packagers: Gulf Power (Alkhorayef, per its site using John Deere, Volvo, Baudouin, Deutz and also Cummins engines), plus Perkins/FG Wilson packagers.

HOW CUMMINS WINS
1. By 3 Oct: ask Dar AlRiyadh (consultant) for the Phase Two electrical spec and approved-vendor list. Ask whether Phase One standardised a genset brand.
2. By 6 Oct: send 60 Hz budget quotes (C2000D6/C2500D6-class paralleled sets for any central generation, plus C500D6-C1000D6 building and pumping-station standby with PowerCommand ATS and paralleling) to Kabbani/Alfanar, Albawani, Shibh Al-Jazira and Alghanim International estimating teams. Also send to any other firm confirmed as qualified.
3. Offer a locally packaged, SASO/LCGPA-compliant configuration and a multi-year O&M/parts package from the Dammam/Eastern branch (Hafr Al-Batin is about 450 km from Dammam).
4. After 20 Oct, track the lowest bidder and lock the MEP subcontractor before the vendor list is frozen.

RISKS
- Phase Two value is unclear. Construction Review cites MEED Projects valuing 'Package 2' at ~$1.36bn and 'Package 1' at ~$783m. $783m matches Phase ONE package 1, so the $1.36bn may be an earlier estimate of Phase One package 2 (awarded at ~$1bn), not the Phase Two tender.
- Power generation may be an extension of the Phase One plant already specified by Alfanar, which gives lock-in.
- The MoD restricted process gives little visibility, and deadlines on MoD tenders often slip.

detail:
WHAT IT IS
Package 14 ('Eastern A Cluster') of National Water Company's long-term operations and maintenance (LTOM) sewage programme, phase two. MEED (28 Apr 2026): 'the Eastern A Cluster (LTOM14) package covers the upgrade of six existing sewage treatment plants with a capacity expansion of 30,000 cubic metres a day (cm/d) at Al Jarodia STP. This will increase total treatment capacity from about 263,000 cubic metres a day (cm/d) to approximately 293,000 cm/d, with an estimated cost of $180m. The bid submission deadline is 30 September.' (https://guest.meed.com/nwc-tenders-next-phase-of-sewage-treatment-programme/). Al-Jarodia is in Qatif governorate (Eastern Province). The other five plant names are not published.

SCOPE CHANGE HISTORY (why sources disagree)
- Before tender, MEED (4 Mar 2026) described LTOM14 as 'the construction of 10 sewage treatment plants' with 'a total capacity of 184,440 cm/d' at $180m (https://guest.meed.com/nwc-to-tender-next-phase-of-sewage-treatment-programme/). Smart Water Magazine (29 Apr) and Global Flow Control (30 Apr) still carry the 10-plant/184,440 figure.
- The tender as issued (MEED 28 Apr, 2 Sep and 4 Sep 2026) is six existing STPs, 263,000 to 293,000 cm/d. MEED also reports NWC 'grouping some upcoming projects': LTOM13 is on hold or merged, and LTOM15 (Eastern B, 2 STPs, 152,000 cm/d) is 'cancelled and has likely been merged'. LTOM16 (Central, 14 STPs) is the next tender, 'potentially in November' (https://guest.meed.com/firms-prepare-bids-for-nwc-sewage-treatment-package-14/).

CONTRACT MODEL (from sister packages)
- LTOM is 'procured on an engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) basis with a long-term operations component' (MEED 13 Mar 2026). Awards go on lowest tariff: LTOM11 went to the consortium that 'offered the lowest tariff'.
- LTOM10 signed 2 Sep 2026: 'SR1.3bn ($347m) ... The 15-year contract ... includes an initial three-year period for rehabilitation and upgrade works, followed by long-term operation and maintenance. NWC said the contract was signed with a tariff of SR0.69 ($0.18) a cubic meter.' (https://guest.meed.com/nwc-confirms-347m-sewage-treatment-plant-deal/). Expect LTOM14 to follow: roughly 3-year rehab plus O&M to year 15, with tariff-based payment (INFERENCE from LTOM10).
- Eastern Province precedent: LTOM7 Al Ahsa (Alkhorayef, SR1.7bn) had 'rehabilitation works ... in two phases within 36 months' and 'O&M ... for 15 years' (https://guest.meed.com/local-contractor-wins-al-ahsa-sewage-package/).
- Financial adviser for the whole programme: Synergy Consulting (MEED 4 Sep 2026).

SCOPE & RATINGS
- No genset schedule is public. NWC's Phase 2 RFQ (https://www.nwc.com.sa/AR/BusinessSector/VendorsRelationships/Documents/NWC%20LTOM%20Phase%202%20-%20RFQ%206.8.2024.pdf) is behind Cloudflare (403) and could not be read.
- INFERENCE: the O&M operator carries the availability and effluent-quality risk for 15 years. It must keep inlet/lift pumping, aeration blowers (partial), UV/chlorination and SCADA running through SEC outages. That means standby diesel at each STP sized for critical process load (not full aeration), typically 0.5-1.5 MW per plant for 20,000-80,000 cm/d plants. The genset split across the six plants is unknown. Some existing sets will be refurbished rather than replaced.
- 60 Hz, 400 V LV (or 13.8 kV MV at larger plants), Eastern Province coastal/humid (Qatif): expect corrosion-protected enclosures and high-ambient radiators (INFERENCE).

DATES & PROCESS
- Tendered April 2026 (restricted RFP to LTOM-qualified firms). Bid submission 30 Sep 2026, i.e. TOMORROW relative to this check (29 Sep). No extension was reported in MEED coverage up to 29 Sep.
- Evaluation: technical, then financial (tariff) opening. LTOM12 financials were opened about 12+ months after the tender, and LTOM12 is still under evaluation. So expect award in H1-H2 2027 (INFERENCE from LTOM11/12 timelines).

COMMERCIAL TERMS
- Estimated cost $180m (MEED). Tariff-based O&M revenue. Bonds and fees are not public (RFP restricted).

ELIGIBILITY
- Bidders come from the NWC LTOM Phase 2 RFQ prequalification (RFQ doc dated 6 Aug 2024 per filename). Named bidders (MEED 4 Sep 2026): Alkhorayef Water & Power Technologies, Civil Works Company, Miahona. United Water/Armada (LTOM10/11 winner) and Beijing Enterprises are NOT bidding.

COMPETITORS (brand via bidder)
- Alkhorayef Water & Power Technologies (AWPT): its sister company Gulf Power ('a proud division of Alkhorayef Group') packages 9-3,400 kVA gensets in Riyadh. Its site shows OEM partners Cummins, Deutz, John Deere, Volvo and Baudouin (https://gulfpower.com.sa/). If AWPT wins, the sets will very likely be Gulf Power packages (INFERENCE). Cummins' play is then to be the ENGINE inside the Gulf Power package, not a competing genset. AWPT is the incumbent LTOM operator in the Eastern Province (Al Ahsa LTOM7) and won three Phase 1 packages worth >SR5.53bn (MEED 12 Feb 2026).
- Civil Works Company (Al-Awael group): partnered with Suez and Veolia on Phase 1 packages. Genset brand unknown. Open to Cat (Zahid), Cummins or Perkins packagers.
- Miahona (Al Muhaidib group, listed): won the Phase 1 Hada/Arana package with Thabat. Genset brand unknown.
- Aggreko / rental firms: temporary power during rehab shutdowns (INFERENCE).

HOW CUMMINS WINS
1. Today (29-30 Sep): the bid is closing, so shift from specification to post-bid positioning. Call the three bidders' procurement leads to confirm Cummins is on their vendor list. Offer a firm unit-rate letter (per-kVA supply plus 15-yr service rate card) they can use in clarifications.
2. Gulf Power: agree an engine-supply price (QSK/QSX 60 Hz engines) so Cummins wins even if AWPT takes LTOM14.
3. Civil Works Co. and Miahona: offer complete 60 Hz standby packages (C500D6-C1500D6 class) with PowerCommand ATS, remote monitoring for SCADA, and a 15-year parts and service agreement from the Dammam branch, with availability guarantees matching NWC penalties.
4. Watch the award (likely 2027), then pitch the winner within the first month of the 3-year rehab.
5. Pipeline: LTOM16 Central (14 STPs) RFP expected November 2026. Pre-position with the same three bidders now.

RISKS
- Bid closes 30 Sep, so there is little chance to influence the offer.
- AWPT has a captive packager (Gulf Power).
- Rehab may reuse existing sets, cutting new-unit volume.
- NWC has repeatedly re-scoped and merged packages.
- Award timelines run 12+ months.

PROJECT TEAM (MEED)
Marriott International (residential operator); Hanmi Global Saudi (PMC); Saudi Diyar Consultants (construction supervision); PLP Architecture (lead design consultant and construction-stage design guardian). The MEP engineer of record is not named. PLP typically works with international MEP engineers, but that is unconfirmed.

SCOPE & RATINGS
- No MEP or genset schedule is public. No bidder list is public.
- Code basis (sourced): SBC 201 §403.4 sets high-rise emergency and standby power requirements, which were significantly changed in the 2024 edition (VortexFire, https://vortexfire.com/insights/sbc-201-801-2024-edition-the-key-changes-you-need-to-know). SBC 801 §1203 covers emergency and standby power systems. Civil Defense approval, including Salamah, is mandatory. SBC 801 requires at least two fire-service access elevators in buildings over 36 m. At 365 m, the tower is far above that threshold, so standby must carry fire pumps, fire-service and occupant-evacuation lifts, smoke control and pressurisation, and emergency lighting (legal basis sourced; load list is INFERENCE based on the IBC-derived SBC).
- Brand standards (INFERENCE): Marriott-branded residences usually add standby for domestic water pumping, some HVAC and lifts beyond code minimum.
- Sizing (ESTIMATE): 242,976 sq m BUA. Code life-safety plus Marriott partial backup at roughly 25-40 W/sq m gives ~6-10 MW. That suggests 3-5 x 2,000-2,500 kWe 60 Hz sets (e.g. C2000D6 / C2500D6-class on QSK60/QSK78) in N+1 paralleled configuration with PowerCommand. A supertall may split sets between the basement and a mid-height or roof plant floor. That split drives fuel transfer, day tanks and flue design, where package engineering can differentiate (INFERENCE).
- Electrical: 60 Hz, likely 13.8 kV SEC supply with LV or MV generation (unconfirmed).

DATES & PROCESS
- Tender issued by 16 Jul 2026 (MEED). Bids due 30 Sep 2026, i.e. tomorrow relative to this check. No extension reported by MEED.
- Private-client tender run by the PMC (Hanmi Global Saudi), not on Etimad. The evaluation basis is not public.
- Genset purchase timing (INFERENCE): the main contractor or its MEP subcontractor will procure gensets 12-24 months after award, once the superstructure is well advanced. So there is a second window after award, at MEP subcontract and vendor-list stage.

COMMERCIAL / ELIGIBILITY
- Bonds, fees and eligibility are not public. PIF real-estate clients usually invite prequalified Tier-1 contractors and ask for ICV/local-content plans (general practice, unverified for this tender).
- Makkah central-area works need Makkah Municipality / Royal Commission for Makkah City and Holy Sites permits and restricted-hours logistics (INFERENCE).

COMPETITORS

Likely Tier-1 high-rise bidders (INFERENCE): Saudi Binladin Group (dominant in the Haram area; also completing Jeddah Tower per MEED https://guest.meed.com/saudi-binladin-group-makes-a-comeback/), China State Construction (CSCEC), El Seif Engineering, Nesma & Partners, and Al-Rashid/other Makkah-focused contractors.
- Genset competitors: Caterpillar via Zahid Tractor (strong in Western Region hotel towers), mtu via packagers, Kohler-SDMO, Perkins/FG Wilson packagers. Brands at nearby Haram-area towers were not found in public sources.

HOW CUMMINS WINS
1. By 1 Oct: email Hanmi Global Saudi (PMC) and Saudi Diyar (supervision) asking whether the specification carries an approved-vendor list for generators. Request that Cummins (locally packaged, SASO-certified) is listed. Offer a technical submittal pack for 60 Hz 2-2.5 MW sets with NFPA 110 Level 1 compliance.
2. By 3 Oct: confirm the bidder list through Hanmi or market contacts. Send budget prices and fuel-system/flue concepts to each bidder's MEP arm for use in post-bid clarifications.
3. After award (likely Q1-Q2 2027): pursue the MEP subcontractor before the genset submittal. Pitch high-rise references, 24/7 Western Region service (Jeddah/Makkah) and a long-term service agreement. Marriott operations value guaranteed response times during Hajj and Ramadan peaks.
4. Use this tower as the entry to Rua Al-Haram's much larger King Salman Gate programme. Register Cummins with Rua's procurement.

WHAT IT IS
A design-and-build contract for Saudi Royal Aviation's (SRA, the government-owned royal flight operator, ICAO code SRA) new aviation complex inside the King Salman International Airport (KSIA) masterplan in Riyadh. MEED (17 Sep 2026): 'Contractors are preparing to submit proposals by 8 October for an estimated SR3bn ($817m) contract ... Government-owned aviation organisation Saudi Royal Aviation (SRA) tendered the contract in August. Phase one of the programme comprised the concept design stage, which has been completed by the design consultant. SRA is now seeking to deliver the second phase, which covers design development, detailed design, procurement, construction, testing, commissioning and close-out of the works. The scope covers 30 landside buildings, including 16 screening areas and gates, in addition to 15 airside buildings, including four gates. The assets include maintenance hangars; workshops; office and administrative buildings – including interior fit-out; warehouses; storage, security and catering facilities; aprons and access roads; and site utilities and civil works. King Salman International airport will provide primary utilities to designated tie-in points, with the contractor taking responsibility from there. While it is within King Salman International airport's boundaries, the site is classified as landside and is a greenfield development. The contractor must therefore meet airport security, safety and access requirements in addition to SRA's own clearance processes.' (https://guest.meed.com/contractors-prepare-riyadh-airport-aviation-complex-bids/). The concept-design consultant is not named publicly.

The same MoH directorate published tender 2026100104 (ref 260939000299) 'إحلال وتأمين مصادر التغذية الإحتياطية لمستشفى حوطة بني تميم بالرياض' on 16 Sep 2026, with identical terms: SAR 1,000 booklet, 18 months, two envelopes, 5% final guarantee, construction classification. Bids close 18 Oct 2026 09:00, expected award 12 Jan 2027. INFERENCE: MoH is running a programme to replace standby power at older hospitals. Tender numbers 2026100102-103 were not in the saved Etimad listing, so they may be other hospitals, closed or not yet public.
- The hospital (sehaguide.com): opened 1426H (about 2005), 'a clinical capacity of 150 beds and 200 beds available', site about 62,500 m2, main building footprint 7,020 m2. It is on King Abdulaziz Road, Al-Udhaybah North, Najran, and is the region's main MoH women's and children's hospital. Web search summaries of SPA/Al-Riyadh reports mention a paediatric floor of 54 beds (29 + 25) and 99 doctors. INFERENCE: the standby plant is original 2005 equipment, now about 20 years old, which fits a like-for-like replacement.

SCOPE & RATINGS
- NOT PUBLIC. The booklet (كراسة الشروط), BOQ and drawings sit behind the Etimad supplier login. The public attachments component (GetAttachmentsViewComponenet) returns an empty 'المرفق' block to visitors. Set count, kVA, voltage, enclosure, tank and ATS scope are not known.
- Etimad classification of the work: activity 'إمدادات الكهرباء والغاز والمياه والبخار وتكييف الهواء' (electricity, gas, water, steam & A/C supply). Work types ticked are 'أعمال الإنشاء' (construction works) and 'أعمال الصيانة والتشغيل' (O&M works). The notice also states 'تشمل المنافسة على بنود توريد: لا' ('the tender includes supply items: No'). So it is set up as a works contract, and the gensets will be bought by the contractor.
- INFERENCE, rating: sizing rules of thumb for a 150-200 bed Saudi general/maternity hospital with central chillers give 2-3 standby diesel sets of about 1,000-2,000 kVA each (total about 2.5-4 MVA). They would be 60 Hz, LV 400/230 V (or legacy 380/220 V), with a synchronising panel and ATSs, a day tank per set and a bulk tank. In KSA the chillers and ICU/NICU/OT loads are usually backed up. MoH specs usually cite NFPA 99/110 (Level 1, Type 10). The code texts were not read, so treat this as an assumption to check against the BOQ. The scope may also include removal of the old sets, new cabling/ATS, O&M during the 18 months and possibly a UPS ('مصادر التغذية' is plural and can include UPS). Confirm in the booklet.

DATES & PROCESS (all from the Etimad visitor page and its components, read 29 Sep 2026)
- Booklet on sale from 14 Sep 2026. Last date for enquiries: 24/09/2026 (13/04/1448), already passed. The page also shows 'بداية إرسال الأسئلة و الاستفسارات 29/09/2026', which contradicts the deadline (Etimad data quirk). The maximum time to answer enquiries is 5 days.

No separate examination date ('تاريخ فحص العروض: لا يوجد'). Standstill period ('فترة التوقف'): 5 days. Expected award 10/01/2027. Works/services start 17/01/2027. Contract duration 18 months, so INFERENCE: completion around July 2028.
- Submission: 'ملفين منفصلين (فني ومالي)', i.e. separate technical and financial envelopes. INFERENCE: technical evaluation comes first and price is opened only for technically compliant bids (the usual GTPL two-envelope process).

COMMERCIAL TERMS
- Booklet price: SAR 1,000.00 ('قيمة وثائق المنافسة 1000.00'). The Etimad listing API field condetionalBookletPrice shows 500. The detail page value of 1,000 is taken as authoritative.
- Initial (bid) guarantee required ('ضمان إبتدائى'), to be delivered to the opening committee, 1st floor, old MoH HQ, King Abdulaziz Rd. Its percentage is in the booklet; INFERENCE: typically 1-2% of the bid value under the Government Tenders & Procurement Law regulations. Final guarantee: 5%. Insurance is not required ('هل التأمين من متطلبات المنافسة: لا').

The earlier SAR 2.5-6M / USD 0.6-1.6M estimate was too low. Full programme award table: tenders_moh_programme.json.

ELIGIBILITY

- Execution site: inside KSA, Najran region, Najran city.
- Local content mechanisms: 'القائمة الإلزامية' (mandatory list of national products) and 'تفضيل المنشآت الصغيرة والمتوسطة' (SME preference). NOT VERIFIED: whether diesel gensets are on the LCGPA mandatory list, because the LCGPA list PDF could not be downloaded here. If they are, the contractor must source a Saudi-made (locally assembled, LCGPA-listed) genset, which favours local packagers. Check lcgpa.gov.sa before quoting.
- Bidders must be Etimad-registered with valid CR, Zakat, GOSI, Chamber and Saudization certificates (standard GTPL requirements, not tender-specific).

COMPETITORS (genset brand behind the contractors)
- Programme winners (Etimad award results): the Al-Rashid group (Abdulrahman Saad Al-Rashid & Sons / Al Rashid Technology & Power) won 6 of 12, and Abdullah Abunayyan Trading (the exclusive Kohler distributor in KSA) won 4 of 12. Noor Energy and Advanced Systems Projects won 1 each. Most low bids fail the technical envelope ('غير مطابق').
- Caterpillar through Zahid Tractor (exclusive Cat dealer in KSA; Zahid also sells FG Wilson/Perkins-engined Cat brands). Zahid has the largest MoH installed base and would be the default 'approved make' in many older MoH specs.
- Saudi local packagers with Perkins, Cummins, mtu or Volvo engines, e.g. Almajd Power (its website says it packages Perkins, Cummins and mtu engines with Deep Sea controls) and Genyard Energy (Perkins 15-2,500 kVA). These score best on the mandatory list and SME preference.
- Kanoo Machinery (Perkins generator distributor in KSA, per kanoomachinery.com/ksa).
- mtu (Rolls-Royce) through its KSA distributor, and Volvo Penta packagers for the smaller sets.
- Al-Bahar is not a factor in KSA. Its Cat territory is UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman and Bahrain.
- Likely prime bidders (INFERENCE): electromechanical contractors from Najran, Abha and Khamis Mushait and Riyadh MEP firms with MoH maintenance experience. The booklet purchaser list is visible only to logged-in suppliers.

HOW CUMMINS WINS
1. Now (by 2 Oct): Cummins Arabia KSA buys the booklet itself (SAR 1,000) from its Etimad supplier account to get the BOQ, drawings and the approved-makes list. INFERENCE: buying a booklet does not require the construction classification; classification is checked at award. It also shows which contractors bought the booklet.
2. By 6 Oct: send a priced turnkey genset package to every booklet buyer. It should include 60 Hz QSK50/QSK60-class standby sets sized to the BOQ, PowerCommand paralleling and ATS, day and bulk tanks, acoustic canopy or room kit, delivery to Najran, commissioning, load-bank test and 18-month O&M. Use one price list for all bidders so Cummins is named in every bid.
3. If the mandatory list covers gensets, supply through a Saudi packager that holds an LCGPA local-content certificate, e.g. a Cummins-engined local package such as Almajd, and keep PowerCommand controls and genuine service.
4. Differentiate on hospital references in KSA, PowerCommand paralleling (NFPA 110 Type 10 transfer), parts availability in the south, and a fixed-price 18-month service offer aligned with the contract's O&M element.
5. After award (expected 10 Jan 2027), close the purchase order with the winning contractor within the 5-day standstill and mobilisation window.

- Older MoH specs may name Cat/Zahid, or 'equal approved'. Get the approved-makes clause from the booklet.
- It is a works contract, so the lowest price among technically compliant bidders wins. Local packagers undercut on price.
- Time is short: 16 days to bid close and the enquiry window has shut, so specification deviations cannot be clarified.
- Hot desert site at about 1,300 m altitude (Najran). INFERENCE: the sets need derating for about 50 C ambient and altitude, which pushes the kVA per set up. Check the site conditions in the spec.

Kuwait Business Gate (mirroring TendersOnTime) lists: 'Procurement Plan For Supply, Installation, And Maintenance Of Electric Generators And Their Accessories ... INFERENCE: the generator line comes from the same MoE plan batch, so the plan was probably drawn up for FY 2025/26-2026/27 and re-published in June 2026.
- There is no CAPT/MoE tender number yet. No live tender matches it in (a) the Indian Embassy Kuwait weekly Kuwait Al-Youm digests, issues 1640-1807 (about 2023 to 30 Sep 2026; 103 PDFs downloaded and text-searched), or (b) all 470 MoE 'practice' notices on bidsgate.moe.edu.kw (BidID 1-470, Sep 2024-Sep 2026).

SCOPE & RATINGS
- NOT PUBLISHED. The plan line says only 'supply, installation and maintenance of electric generators and their accessories'.
- INFERENCE: sets at MoE sites in Kuwait's six educational districts (Capital, Hawalli, Farwaniya, Ahmadi, Jahra, Mubarak Al-Kabeer): schools, MoE headquarters (new HQ in South Surra), stores in South Sabhan, and possibly exam/control centres. Kuwait supply is 50 Hz, 415/240 V (MEW regulations).
- INFERENCE: KWD 700,000 (about USD 2.27M) including maintenance would buy roughly 15-40 sets in the 100-500 kVA class plus ATS, cabling and a 1-3 year maintenance tail. It could also be a smaller number of 1-2 MVA sets for MoE HQ or data centres. The mix will only be known from the CAPT/MoE documents.
- Context (INFERENCE): the 2026 regional conflict (Kuwait reports missile/drone interceptions in September 2026, per the Kuwait Business Gate news ticker) and summer load-shedding raise the priority of standby power at schools and MoE buildings.

DATES & PROCESS
- The float date is not announced. INFERENCE: Kuwait's fiscal year runs April to March, so a line in the 2026/27 plan should float before 31 Mar 2027.
- It could come through either channel:
  (a) CAPT public tender, numbered 'ME/nn/2026/2027'. The digests show MoE tenders under this prefix, e.g. 'TENDER NO. ME/23/2025/2026 ... MINISTRY OF EDUCATION ... Relevant Fee KD 3500/- ... Initial Guarantee KD 62,000/- valid for 90 days in favor of CAPT'. CAPT timing is typically 6-12 weeks from document sale to closing, with a pre-tender meeting.
  (b) MoE 'practice' (ممارسة), numbered 'م م/nn/2026-2027', on bidsgate.moe.edu.kw. Practices close 10 working days after publication, with a pre-tender meeting the following Sunday.
- INFERENCE: KWD 700k is above the value MoE normally handles by practice, so route (a) CAPT is more likely.
- Watch list: CAPT 'opening tenders' filtered to MoE (capt.gov.kw returns 403 from this environment, so check from a Kuwait browser); the Indian Embassy weekly digest (indembkwt.gov.in/pdf/Tenders Issue NNNN.pdf, every Monday); and bidsgate.moe.edu.kw/BidsList.

COMMERCIAL TERMS (expected, from comparable MoE notices; not tender-specific)
- CAPT route: document fee KD 75-3,500 depending on size (ME/23/2025/2026 was KD 3,500 with a KD 62,000 bid bond for a large O&M job). Initial guarantee is a fixed KD amount valid 90 days in favour of CAPT. INFERENCE: roughly KD 7,000-14,000 (1-2%) for a KD 700k job. Final guarantee is typically 10% in Kuwait (not verified for this tender). Offers are valid 90 days.
- MoE practice route (verbatim from MoE practice M.M/25/2026-2027): 'المقابل المادي للحصول على نسخة من وثائق الممارسة ... (75) ... دينار', 'تأمين أولي لا يقل عن ... 2000 د.ك' as a certified cheque or bank LG from a Kuwaiti bank in favour of MoE. Bank guarantees must be in Arabic. Offers go to the tender box at the Supplies & Stores Dept, South Sabhan.

ELIGIBILITY
- MoE practices are open only to 'الممارسين المعتمدين لدى وزارة التربية' (MoE-certified bidders). The bidder must be a specialised company inside Kuwait, registered in the Commercial Registry and Kuwait Chamber of Commerce for the current year, with relevant experience and trained technical staff.
- CAPT tenders require CAPT registration in the matching category. Standard CAPT and KISR notices also require a National Manpower (PAM) certificate and a PAM 'to whom it may concern' certificate showing the company file is not suspended. SMEs get a fee exemption.
- A foreign OEM cannot bid directly. INFERENCE: Cummins Arabia's Kuwait entity (formerly GTE, part of the Cummins Arabia JV per cummins.com) can bid if it holds CAPT/MoE registration. Otherwise it supplies a registered Kuwaiti electromechanical contractor.

PAST MoE GENERATOR TENDERS

COMPETITORS

- mtu through Al Mulla Power Solutions, the authorised mtu distributor in Kuwait. It claims '200+ mtu units' in Kuwait including '45 Series 4000 gensets at Kuwait International Airport' and Jahra Hospital.
- Perkins through Al-Nisf Equipment Co (authorised Perkins parts distributor in Kuwait) and local packagers such as Ali Al Dousari (DME Generators, Perkins gensets).

- MoE award is generally the lowest compliant price.

HOW CUMMINS WINS
1. This month, confirm registration. Does Cummins Arabia Kuwait hold CAPT registration in the electrical/generator category and MoE 'certified bidder' status on bidsgate.moe.edu.kw? If not, apply now; it is the gating item.
2. Ask the MoE Maintenance Dept (إدارة الصيانة) / Educational Facilities sector for the scope: sites, kVA and whether maintenance covers existing sets and their makes.

4. Line up 2-3 MoE-registered Kuwaiti contractors with exclusive pricing in case MoE requires a local contractor.

- mtu/Al Mulla and Cat/Al-Bahar have a strong Kuwaiti government installed base.

WHAT IT IS
- DEWA open tender No. 2132600053: 'UPGRADATION OF STANDBY GENERATORS AT DISTRIBUTION CONTROL CENTER, QUASIS ON PLOT NO. 232-552 AND UPGRADATION OF STANDBY GENERATORS AT DISTRIBUTION CONTROL CENTER, WARSAN SECOND ON PLOT NO. 622-159'. Floating date 19-May-2026. Closing date 30-Jul-2026 (originally 02-Jul-2026 per TendersArabia TA-141576625 and TendersOnTime 141601730/141576625; extended per TA-144445009). Tender type: Open Tender. Offers were submitted online through DEWA SRM ('Tenderers are required to submit their offers online').
- The sites are DEWA's two electricity distribution control centres, which run Dubai's 33/11 kV network.
  - Warsan: DEWA (16 Oct 2011) described the Warsan centre as 'two buildings - one for electricity distribution control with the capacity of 33 KV and 11 KV, and the other for monitoring and controlling electricity generation and transmission (400/132 kV)'.
  - Al Qusais: 'the Control Centre at Al Qusais, which cost AED 29 million ... consists of two floors and includes distribution, planning, and coordination departments ... a simulator, and on-site distribution management' (Emirates 24|7 / Utilities ME, 22-23 Jan 2014). The two centres run as a 'Multi-Site System' backing each other up in an emergency.
  - Both opened in January 2014. INFERENCE: the standby sets being upgraded are about 12-13 years old (installed around 2012-2013).

STATUS & BIDS (DEWA Tender Opening Results page, saved 29 Sep 2026; seven offers, not six)
 01 DANWAY LLC: AED 7,497,000.00; '13 MONTHS INCLUDING 15 DAYS MOBILISATION'; bank guarantee RECEIVED; online offer.
 02 GALADARI ENERGY SOLUTIONS LLC: AED 3,872,910.00 (lowest); completion blank; bank guarantee RECEIVED.
 03 KANOO ENERGY L.L.C: AED 6,300,000.00; '40 WEEKS'; bank guarantee RECEIVED.

 06 JUBAILI BROS. LLC: 'REGRET'.
 07 AL MASAOOD L.L.C.: 'REGRET'. Al Masaood is the mtu (Rolls-Royce Power Systems) distributor in the UAE.
- No award is published yet; there was no award notice on DEWA's page at 29 Sep 2026. The DEWA page says: 'The Total Price(s) and details of the offers ... are as indicated by the Tenderers ... no request for any further information about any offer shall be entertained.'
- Award timing, INFERENCE: DEWA runs technical evaluation and then commercial evaluation. With opening on 30 Jul 2026 and a typical 2-4 month evaluation, the award is likely in Oct-Nov 2026, possibly within weeks. Delivery or completion is 13 months or 40 weeks from award, so gensets would be needed on site about Q2-Q3 2027.

SCOPE & RATINGS
- NOT PUBLIC. Set count, kVA, voltage, enclosure, fuel system and ATS/sync scope are in the DEWA SRM tender documents, which are login-only.
- INFERENCE from building type and bid values: each DCC probably has 2 (N+1) or 3 sets, each about 800-2,000 kVA, 50 Hz, 400/230 V LV (or 11 kV), with paralleling/synchronising switchboards, AMF/ATS, day and bulk tanks, and stack/acoustic works. 'Upgradation' can mean full replacement plus controls, or re-engining or controls retrofit. The 13-month durations and AED 3.9-10.7M prices point to replacement of the sets plus electrical and civil works at two live sites.
- Genset share, INFERENCE: about 40-60% of contract value, i.e. AED 1.5-4.5M (USD 0.4-1.2M).

COMMERCIAL TERMS
- Online submission on DEWA SRM, and a tender bond (bank guarantee) was required: DEWA shows 'Bank Guarante RECEIVED' for the five priced offers.
- The bond amount (AED 200,000 in the earlier record) is NOT VERIFIED. The public TendersArabia TA-144445009 page shows no bond ('Tender Value: Refer Document', 'Document Cost: 0.00'). The document fee shows as 0.00 AED on TendersArabia.

ELIGIBILITY
- The public notice says: open tender, bidders registered as DEWA suppliers on SRM. Licensing class and genset approved-makes list are not public. INFERENCE: DEWA specs for critical facilities usually require an OEM with local service and DEWA-approved makes; check the approved vendor list.

BIDDERS AND THEIR LIKELY GENSET BRANDS (sourced where stated; otherwise INFERENCE)
- Galadari Energy Solutions (L1). A Galadari Brothers subsidiary and distributor of Atlas Copco and Baudouin. Its own 'GES' generators are 'powered by Baudouin engines' (galadarienergy.com/brand/ges; the page title also says 'Komatsu and Perkins Generators in UAE'). INFERENCE: its AED 3.87M price almost certainly uses GES/Baudouin sets, so Cummins cannot supply this bidder unless DEWA's approved-makes list forces a change.
- Kanoo Energy L.L.C (L2). Part of the Kanoo group (Kanoo Industrial & Energy). Its sister company Kanoo Machinery 'exclusively manages the business for Perkins engines across the Middle East region'. INFERENCE: likely Perkins-engined sets, probably through Kanoo Machinery. The 40-week delivery fits imported 4000-series lead times. The earlier record's 'Cat-linked' wording is imprecise: Perkins is Caterpillar-owned, but the UAE Cat dealer is Al-Bahar.
- Precision Industries LLC (L3). A Dubai genset OEM in Al Quoz, founded 2005 (Beta Holding). Its site states: 'Cummins & Perkins Authorised Official Sales & Service Partner'; 'strategic agreements with ... Cummins, Stamford, and Leroy-Somer in 2014 and Perkins in 2017'; product filter lists Perkins (171), Cummins (55), Yuchai (72), Mitsubishi (19) models; range 10-4,000 kVA. This is the natural Cummins channel. Which engine it quoted is unknown.
- Danway LLC (L4). A Dubai electrical and mechanical contractor with DEWA 132/11 kV substation track record ('energized its 24th 132/11KV ... Substation in the DEWA network'). It has no own genset brand, so the OEM is open (INFERENCE).
- Yukon International Contracting LLC (L5, highest). A Deira-based EPCC/MEP contractor (est. 2017). No genset brand; OEM open (INFERENCE).
- Jubaili Bros (regret). A genset manufacturer with its own brand.
- Al Masaood (regret). The mtu distributor, so mtu is not a direct bidder.
- Al-Bahar (Cat dealer for UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain) did not bid directly.

HOW CUMMINS WINS (per bidder)
1. Precision Industries (priority): confirm this week whether PI's offer is Cummins-engined. If it is, lock in engine, alternator and PowerCommand pricing, delivery slots and DEWA-grade service commitments so PI can hold price through clarification. If it quoted Perkins or Yuchai, offer a Cummins QSK-based alternative at matched price for any DEWA-requested re-offer or post-award substitution.
2. Kanoo Energy (L2): offer Cummins as a faster-delivery or approved-make alternative if Galadari is disqualified technically. Kanoo is likely tied to Perkins, so the odds are low to medium.
3. Galadari (L1): low odds. The only opening is if DEWA's technical evaluation rejects the Baudouin/GES offer or requires an approved make; have a compliant Cummins package ready to pitch to the next-ranked bidders.
4. Danway / Yukon: brand-neutral contractors. Send full Cummins package pricing in case the award goes past L1-L3 on technical grounds, and use the contact for future DEWA MEP work.
5. DEWA side: make sure Cummins gensets are on DEWA Distribution's approved list. Point to DEWA's existing Cummins EDG fleet: DEWA RFQ 2412601624 (23 Sep 2026, 'CUMMINS SPARES', delivery 'H1 STORES, WARSAN') and RFQ 2012605085 cover spares for Cummins C1675 D5 / KTA50-G8, KTA38-G5, KTA19-G4 and VTA28-G5 EDGs at the Ruler's palaces. Also offer PowerCommand paralleling suited to the 'Multi-Site' control-centre philosophy.

RISKS
- The L1 (Galadari/Baudouin) price is 39% below L2. If it is technically compliant, DEWA will award to it and Cummins is out.
- Award may be imminent, so there is little time for re-specification.
- The actual scope may be controls retrofit or re-engining rather than new sets (unknown).
- The bond amount and spec remain unverified.
